modelTitle: How Hospitals Pay Agents by the Interaction.
modelParagraphs: Hippocratic AI sells patient-facing clinical agents to hospitals and health systems on enterprise contracts — agents that handle non-diagnostic tasks like appointment prep, medication reminders, follow-up check-ins and chronic-care outreach, staffed against the roughly 1.2 million-nurse shortfall in the U.S. Healthcare organizations pay per deployment and per interaction volume rather than per seat.

The 2025 app store opened a second channel: clinicians design and publish their own agents, and Hippocratic takes the underlying platform spend. Series C funds were earmarked for M&A, product development and international expansion — a signal that the company is consolidating the patient-communication stack while revenue remains below disclosure scale.

faqs.q: What Is Hippocratic AI's ARR in 2026?
faqs.a: Hippocratic AI has not precisely disclosed its ARR. It is carried here at an estimated ~$50 million threshold, consistent with third-party research; the company's most concrete traction numbers are 10 million+ patient calls and a $3.5 billion valuation.

faqs.q: Why Is Hippocratic AI's Revenue Only an Estimate?
faqs.a: The company has never published revenue, margin or burn figures. Its funding rounds — $141M Series B at $1.64B in January 2025 and $126M Series C at $3.5B in November 2025 — are the primary public signals, and analysts derive revenue context from those multiples.

faqs.q: How Does Hippocratic AI Make Money?
faqs.a: Enterprise contracts with hospitals and health systems for patient-facing, non-diagnostic agents — priced per deployment and per interaction — plus an app store where clinicians build agents and Hippocratic monetizes the underlying platform usage.
$3.5 billion after a $126 million Series C led by Avenir Growth on November 3, 2025, up from $1.64 billion at the January 2025 Series B. Total funding stands at $404 million across six rounds.

faqs.q: What Does Hippocratic AI Actually Do?
faqs.a: It builds safety-focused generative AI agents for patient-facing healthcare communication — appointment prep, medication reminders, follow-ups and chronic-care check-ins — positioned against the roughly 1.2 million-nurse shortage in U.S. healthcare, with expansion into nurse workflows and life sciences in 2026.
